title: Arrears, Suspension and Reinstatement on a Northbeam Credit Account
content:
An account of the Northbeam Store Credit and Financing Accounts range is not treated as delinquent before the product's delinquency days have run from the day the minimum payment fell due.

## 1. Counting the days

Delinquency days are counted as calendar days from the payment due day, which counts as day zero, and a due day falling on a day the banks are shut moves to the next banking day. The count is read against the account's own record of the day the payment fell due and of the least payment the statement asked for, and it is read before the account is treated as delinquent.

The count is a not-before test taken inclusively: on the day that falls the product's delinquency days after the due day the account may be treated as delinquent, and on the day before that it may not. A day earlier in the count, however far the arrears have run in other respects, does not satisfy it.

## 2. The late fee

The product's late fee is charged once the product's late fee grace days have run past the due day, and it is charged once per statement period however many payments are missed in it.

## 3. Suspension

Spending is suspended when utilisation passes the product's suspension figure, when the account is delinquent, or when unauthorised use is suspected. Suspension does not close the account and the balance stays payable. Each of the three grounds stands on its own: any one of them is enough, and none of them requires the others.

## 4. Reporting and coming back

The arrears are reported to the credit bureaux once the product's reporting days have run, and the account is brought back only on what the product's cure basis requires. An account brought back spends again.

## 5. A returned payment

A returned payment carries the product's returned payment fee. A payment returned after the account was reinstated puts it back into delinquency on the original due day rather than a fresh one, so the count that had already run is not started again.

## 6. Points of judgement on the counting

- Where the payment due day falls on a day the banks are shut, the due day itself is the next banking day, and the calendar days are counted from that day as day zero.
- The delinquency count, the late fee count and the reporting count all run from the due day, each to the number of days its own figure gives.
- Two accounts whose payments fell due on the same day, held on products whose delinquency days differ, reach delinquency on different days, because the count is the product's own.
